**Demand is deterministic.** Identical prices always gave identical results.

**Demand model:** ln q ≈ ln(anchor q) − b·Δp + c·Δgap, where gap = competitor price − my price.
- Equal-price anchors: 1.48 gave 47.06, 1.49 gave 46.95, 1.50 gave 46.83, 1.51 gave 46.71. 1.47 is about 47.18 (estimated). So b ≈ 0.25 near 1.5.
- Own-price slope s = b + c (competitor fixed): about 2.1–2.2 near a zero gap. Estimates were 2.13 at R79, 2.10 at R83, and 2.17 at R87.
- c, the gap effect, saturates as the gap widens:
  - about 1.8–1.9 near a zero gap
  - about 1.6 on gaps 0.02–0.12
  - about 1.17 on gaps 0.12–0.23
  - about 0.82 on gaps 0.23–0.31
- Negative gaps (me above the competitor) cost heavily: R35 and R42.
- b, the own-price slope at a fixed gap:
  - about 1.0 near 1.9
  - about 0.72 on 1.77–1.84
  - about 0.48 on 1.67–1.72
  - about 0.25–0.3 on 1.48–1.53

**Best response:** p − 1 ≈ 1/s ≈ 0.46–0.48. Profit curves are very flat (within about 0.03 over ±0.01). Do not follow the competitor below 1.46.

**Demand model:** ln q ≈ ln(anchor q) − b·Δp + c·Δgap, where gap = competitor price − my price.
- Equal-price anchors: 1.48 gave 47.06, 1.49 gave 46.95, 1.50 gave 46.83, 1.51 gave 46.71. 1.47 is about 47.18 (estimated). So b ≈ 0.25 near 1.5.

- c, the gap effect, saturates as the gap widens:
  - about 1.8–1.9 near a zero gap
  - about 1.6 on gaps 0.02–0.12
  - about 1.17 on gaps 0.12–0.23
  - about 0.82 on gaps 0.23–0.31
- Negative gaps (me above the competitor) cost heavily: R35 and R42.
- b, the own-price slope at a fixed gap:
  - about 1.0 near 1.9
  - about 0.72 on 1.77–1.84
  - about 0.48 on 1.67–1.72
  - about 0.25–0.3 on 1.48–1.53

**Demand is deterministic.** Identical prices always gave identical results.

**Demand model:** ln q ≈ ln(anchor q) − b·Δp + c·Δgap, where gap = competitor price − my price.
- Equal-price anchors: 1.48 gave 47.06, 1.49 gave 46.95, 1.50 gave 46.83, 1.51 gave 46.71. 1.47 is about 47.18 (estimated). So b ≈ 0.25 near 1.5.
- Own-price slope s = b + c (competitor fixed): about 2.1–2.2 near a zero gap. Estimates were 2.13 at R79, 2.10 at R83, and 2.17 at R87.
- c, the gap effect, saturates as the gap widens:
  - about 1.8–1.9 near a zero gap
  - about 1.6 on gaps 0.02–0.12
  - about 1.17 on gaps 0.12–0.23
  - about 0.82 on gaps 0.23–0.31
- Negative gaps (me above the competitor) cost heavily: R35 and R42.
- b, the own-price slope at a fixed gap:
  - about 1.0 near 1.9
  - about 0.72 on 1.77–1.84
  - about 0.48 on 1.67–1.72
  - about 0.25–0.3 on 1.48–1.53

**Best response:** p − 1 ≈ 1/s ≈ 0.46–0.48. Profit curves are very flat (within about 0.03 over ±0.01). Do not follow the competitor below 1.46.

**Demand is deterministic.** Identical prices always gave identical results.

**Demand model:** ln q ≈ ln(anchor q) − b·Δp + c·Δgap, where gap = competitor price − my price.
- Equal-price anchors: 1.48 gave 47.06, 1.49 gave 46.95, 1.50 gave 46.83, 1.51 gave 46.71. 1.47 is about 47.18 (estimated). So b ≈ 0.25 near 1.5.
- Own-price slope s = b + c (competitor fixed): about 2.1–2.2 near a zero gap. Estimates were 2.13 at R79, 2.10 at R83, and 2.17 at R87.
- c, the gap effect, saturates as the gap widens:
  - about 1.8–1.9 near a zero gap
  - about 1.6 on gaps 0.02–0.12
  - about 1.17 on gaps 0.12–0.23
  - about 0.82 on gaps 0.23–0.31
- Negative gaps (me above the competitor) cost heavily: R35 and R42.
- b, the own-price slope at a fixed gap:
  - about 1.0 near 1.9
  - about 0.72 on 1.77–1.84
  - about 0.48 on 1.67–1.72
  - about 0.25–0.3 on 1.48–1.53

**Best response:** p − 1 ≈ 1/s ≈ 0.46–0.48. Profit curves are very flat (within about 0.03 over ±0.01). Do not follow the competitor below 1.46.

**Demand is deterministic.** Identical prices always gave identical results.

**Demand model:** ln q ≈ ln(anchor q) − b·Δp + c·Δgap, where gap = competitor price − my price.
- Equal-price anchors: 1.48 gave 47.06, 1.49 gave 46.95, 1.50 gave 46.83, 1.51 gave 46.71. 1.47 is about 47.18 (estimated). So b ≈ 0.25 near 1.5.
- Own-price slope s = b + c (competitor fixed): about 2.1–2.2 near a zero gap. Estimates were 2.13 at R79, 2.10 at R83, and 2.17 at R87.
- c, the gap effect, saturates as the gap widens:
  - about 1.8–1.9 near a zero gap
  - about 1.6 on gaps 0.02–0.12
  - about 1.17 on gaps 0.12–0.23
  - about 0.82 on gaps 0.23–0.31
- Negative gaps (me above the competitor) cost heavily: R35 and R42.
- b, the own-price slope at a fixed gap:
  - about 1.0 near 1.9
  - about 0.72 on 1.77–1.84
  - about 0.48 on 1.67–1.72
  - about 0.25–0.3 on 1.48–1.53

**Best response:** p − 1 ≈ 1/s ≈ 0.46–0.48. Profit curves are very flat (within about 0.03 over ±0.01). Do not follow the competitor below 1.46.

**Demand model:** ln q ≈ ln(anchor q) − b·Δp + c·Δgap, where gap = competitor price − my price.
- Equal-price anchors: 1.48 gave 47.06, 1.49 gave 46.95, 1.50 gave 46.83, 1.51 gave 46.71. 1.47 is about 47.18 (estimated). So b ≈ 0.25 near 1.5.

- c, the gap effect, saturates as the gap widens:
  - about 1.8–1.9 near a zero gap
  - about 1.6 on gaps 0.02–0.12
  - about 1.17 on gaps 0.12–0.23
  - about 0.82 on gaps 0.23–0.31
- Negative gaps (me above the competitor) cost heavily: R35 and R42.
- b, the own-price slope at a fixed gap:
  - about 1.0 near 1.9
  - about 0.72 on 1.77–1.84
  - about 0.48 on 1.67–1.72
  - about 0.25–0.3 on 1.48–1.53

**Best response:** p − 1 ≈ 1/s ≈ 0.46–0.48. Profit curves are very flat (within about 0.03 over ±0.01). Do not follow the competitor below 1.46.

**Demand is deterministic.** Identical prices always gave identical results.

**Demand model:** ln q ≈ ln(anchor q) − b·Δp + c·Δgap, where gap = competitor price − my price.
- Equal-price anchors: 1.48 gave 47.06, 1.49 gave 46.95, 1.50 gave 46.83, 1.51 gave 46.71. 1.47 is about 47.18 (estimated). So b ≈ 0.25 near 1.5.
- Own-price slope s = b + c (competitor fixed): about 2.1–2.2 near a zero gap. Estimates were 2.13 at R79, 2.10 at R83, and 2.17 at R87.
- c, the gap effect, saturates as the gap widens:
  - about 1.8–1.9 near a zero gap
  - about 1.6 on gaps 0.02–0.12
  - about 1.17 on gaps 0.12–0.23
  - about 0.82 on gaps 0.23–0.31
- Negative gaps (me above the competitor) cost heavily: R35 and R42.
- b, the own-price slope at a fixed gap:
  - about 1.0 near 1.9
  - about 0.72 on 1.77–1.84
  - about 0.48 on 1.67–1.72
  - about 0.25–0.3 on 1.48–1.53

**Best response:** p − 1 ≈ 1/s ≈ 0.46–0.48. Profit curves are very flat (within about 0.03 over ±0.01). Do not follow the competitor below 1.46.

**Demand is deterministic.** Identical prices always gave identical results.

**Demand model:** ln q ≈ ln(anchor q) − b·Δp + c·Δgap, where gap = competitor price − my price.
- Equal-price anchors: 1.48 gave 47.06, 1.49 gave 46.95, 1.50 gave 46.83, 1.51 gave 46.71. 1.47 is about 47.18 (estimated). So b ≈ 0.25 near 1.5.
- Own-price slope s = b + c (competitor fixed): about 2.1–2.2 near a zero gap. Estimates were 2.13 at R79, 2.10 at R83, and 2.17 at R87.
- c, the gap effect, saturates as the gap widens:
  - about 1.8–1.9 near a zero gap
  - about 1.6 on gaps 0.02–0.12
  - about 1.17 on gaps 0.12–0.23
  - about 0.82 on gaps 0.23–0.31
- Negative gaps (me above the competitor) cost heavily: R35 and R42.
- b, the own-price slope at a fixed gap:
  - about 1.0 near 1.9
  - about 0.72 on 1.77–1.84
  - about 0.48 on 1.67–1.72
  - about 0.25–0.3 on 1.48–1.53

**Best response:** p − 1 ≈ 1/s ≈ 0.46–0.48. Profit curves are very flat (within about 0.03 over ±0.01). Do not follow the competitor below 1.46.

**Demand is deterministic.** Identical prices always gave identical results.

**Demand model:** ln q ≈ ln(anchor q) − b·Δp + c·Δgap, where gap = competitor price − my price.
- Equal-price anchors: 1.48 gave 47.06, 1.49 gave 46.95, 1.50 gave 46.83, 1.51 gave 46.71. 1.47 is about 47.18 (estimated). So b ≈ 0.25 near 1.5.
- Own-price slope s = b + c (competitor fixed): about 2.1–2.2 near a zero gap. Estimates were 2.13 at R79, 2.10 at R83, and 2.17 at R87.
- c, the gap effect, saturates as the gap widens:
  - about 1.8–1.9 near a zero gap
  - about 1.6 on gaps 0.02–0.12
  - about 1.17 on gaps 0.12–0.23
  - about 0.82 on gaps 0.23–0.31
- Negative gaps (me above the competitor) cost heavily: R35 and R42.
- b, the own-price slope at a fixed gap:
  - about 1.0 near 1.9
  - about 0.72 on 1.77–1.84
  - about 0.48 on 1.67–1.72
  - about 0.25–0.3 on 1.48–1.53

**Best response:** p − 1 ≈ 1/s ≈ 0.46–0.48. Profit curves are very flat (within about 0.03 over ±0.01). Do not follow the competitor below 1.46.
